title: Base change of an indexed coproduct of copies of a scheme
statement: Let $U$ and $V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $v:V\to U$ be a morphism, let $E$ be a set, and let $U_E=\coprod_{e\in E}U$ and $V_E=\coprod_{e\in E}V$ be the coproducts of copies of the schemes [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with codiagonals to $U$ and $V$. Then the morphism of schemes over $V$ $$V_E\longrightarrow V\times_U U_E$$ whose restriction to the $e$-th summand is the unique morphism with projections $\operatorname{id}_V:V\to V$ and $\iota_e\circ v:V\to U_E$ is an isomorphism. Under this isomorphism, the $e$-th coprojection of $V_E$ corresponds to the base change of the $e$-th coprojection of $U_E$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes), applied to the coproduct family after base change, with the universal property of fibre products in Section 26.17

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the coprojections of $U_E$ and $V_E$ are open immersions with pairwise disjoint images covering their targets; hence each summand is open and closed. For every $e$, the pair of maps $\operatorname{id}_V:V\to V$ and $\iota_e\circ v:V\to U_E$ has equal composites to $U$, so the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a unique map $j_e:V\to V\times_U U_E$ over $V$. The maps $j_e$ assemble, by the coproduct universal property, to the displayed morphism $j:V_E\to V\times_UU_E$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes), with the universal property of fibre products

proof.text: For each $e$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to the open subscheme $\iota_e(U)\subseteq U_E$ and the identity open subscheme of $V$: it identifies $V\times_U\iota_e(U)\cong V\times_UU\cong V$ with the open subscheme $W_e=q^{-1}(\iota_e(U))$ of $V\times_UU_E$, and the resulting open immersion $V\to V\times_UU_E$ has projections $\operatorname{id}_V$ and $\iota_e\circ v$, so by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] it is $j_e$, the base change of $\iota_e$; thus $j_e$ is an isomorphism $V\to W_e$. The $W_e$ are pairwise disjoint because the $\iota_e(U)$ are, and they cover $V\times_UU_E$ because every point of $U_E$ lies in one $\iota_e(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] applied to the open covering $(W_e)_{e\in E}$ (the overlap condition is vacuous for $e\ne e'$), the morphisms $\iota'_e\circ j_e^{-1}:W_e\to V_E$, with $\iota'_e$ the coprojections of $V_E$, glue to $g:V\times_UU_E\to V_E$. Then $g\circ j\circ\iota'_e=\iota'_e$ for every $e$, so $g\circ j=\operatorname{id}$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; and $j\circ g$ restricts to the inclusion on every $W_e$, so $j\circ g=\operatorname{id}$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Thus $j$ is an isomorphism, and its restriction to the $e$-th summand is exactly the base change of $\iota_e$.
